title: Fair distinctions make percolation
claim: For not-all-equal constraints NAE(h_u, x_e, h_v) with uniformly random visible spokes x on a finite multigraph: (1) for any two-colouring g, tau = h xor g makes them equivalent to uniformly random implications on bichromatic edges and uniformly random monotone two-literal clauses on monochromatic (seam) edges; (2) in a uniformly random orientation the set reachable from any vertex set has the law of its bond-percolation cluster at p = 1/2, and with independently oriented gadgets at the gadget's traversal probability (series of blocks of k_i parallel edges: product of 1 - 2^-k_i); (3) if the seam joins disjoint sides T and B and no directed path runs from B to T (or from T to B), the world is consistent, so inconsistency needs crossings both ways and P(consistent) >= 1 - P_perc(B connected to T), while worlds crossed both ways can be consistent; (4) on tori of fixed shape cut along one seam: emergence tends to 0 exponentially when the traversal probability is below the lattice's bond threshold (honeycomb; series gadgets), stays bounded on the square lattice with plain edges (Russo-Seymour-Welsh), and tends to infinity on the square lattice with k >= 3 parallel edges, whose two-way gadgets percolate. The lower bound at the critical point is open.
failure_conditions: A graph, colouring and spoke pattern where the world and its recoloured instance differ in consistency, or an edge whose two spoke values give the same form.
A small graph or decorated graph where the reach law differs from percolation at the stated parameter, or a gadget probability that differs from its formula.
A cut-open torus pattern blocked in one direction that is inconsistent, or a torus where crossed-both-ways worlds are never consistent.
foundation_claim_scope: Satisfiability of not-all-equal worlds with hidden joints and fair visible distinctions on graphs embedded in the torus, reduced to random orientations and bond percolation. Lattices are declared; no space is constructed and no physical claim is made.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py verifies the recolouring on five graphs for three colourings and every spoke pattern (786,432 cases on the 3 x 3 torus), exact equality of reach and percolation laws on three plain and four decorated graphs with the gadget probabilities, and the blocking theorem on every pattern of the 3 x 2 and 5 x 2 tori and 200,000 of the 3 x 4 torus, with consistent two-way worlds present; four controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive checks of Theorems 1-3; Theorem 4 (regimes) argued in prose from cited percolation theorems (Kesten; Menshikov; Aizenman-Barsky; Wierman; Russo-Seymour-Welsh; Harris; standard supercritical facts); the coupling is that of Grimmett's randomly oriented lattice; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found for the gauge recolouring and the reach-percolation coupling (Grimmett 2001); candidate-local-delta for the reduction of not-all-equal worlds and their emergence at scale to percolation at an effective parameter, the blocking theorem with the failure of its converse, and the three regimes. Bounded search: random two-literal instances and implication-digraph percolation on random graphs (Chvatal-Reed; Bollobas et al.), no lattice version found.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-22.
